bullets.title: Futures bid: S&P +0.4-0.5%, yields pinned at 5.27%, crude -2% to $87
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures up 0.4-0.5% and Nasdaq up ~60bps pre-market as bond yields stabilized (-3bps to 5.27% on 10yr) and WTI crude dropped ~2% to $87.21, easing cost pressures. The tape is near record highs — S&P just 0.3% below all-time close, Nasdaq already at new records — despite 10- and 30-year yields at highest levels since 2002. JPM returned to a tactically bullish view, noting October rate hike expectations fell from 64% to 22% and Q3 earnings are expected to show 29.5% EPS growth.

bullets.title: Meta Muse agentic AI is the dominant theme: CPU TAM seen 10x-ing to $300B by 2030
bullets.body: Citi, Mizuho, and MS are all converging on the view that Meta's Muse personal AI agent — 6.6M downloads, 1.8M DAUs, #1 app for 16 consecutive days — represents a structural shift in compute demand. CPU TAM is projected to expand from $29B (2025) to $300B (2030) as always-on agents consume 5-30x more tokens per task than chatbots; agentic server workloads seen rising from 4% to 30% of shipments by 2030. Citi projects Muse itself could generate $27B+ in transaction-take-rate revenue at scale across $16.5T of addressable commerce verticals.

bullets.title: Citi raises AMD to $800, NVDA Buy $315 as primary semiconductor beneficiaries of agentic AI
bullets.body: Citi's Atif Malik raised AMD's price target to $800, citing AMD as the primary CPU beneficiary of Meta's Muse agents given Meta is one of AMD's largest server customers. NVDA reiterated Buy at $315: 100M Muse DAUs alone would require 200K–390K Blackwell GPUs worth $7–19B in one-time revenue, with each incremental million agentic DAUs worth $70–190M to Nvidia. AMD CEO Lisa Su confirmed the company plans to 'substantially increase' supply in 2027 with 'very high' demand expected for several years.

bullets.title: GOOGL + CEG: 890 MW, 20-year nuclear deal confirmed; $4.3B+ investment
bullets.body: Google and Constellation Energy confirmed a 20-year PPA for 890 MW of new nuclear capacity across 11 units in Illinois, Pennsylvania, and New Jersey on the PJM grid, with first uprate by 2028 and a $4.3B+ Constellation buildout commitment. An additional 15-year supply agreement covers 2,700 MW from Constellation's existing fleet. CEG was up ~8.4% pre-market on the news; the deal is emblematic of hyperscalers locking in long-duration, carbon-free power ahead of multi-GW AI data center buildouts (Amazon signed 690MW at Calvert Cliffs; Microsoft restarted Three Mile Island).

bullets.title: TSMC FY26 guide heading to low-to-mid 40s% revenue growth; 2027 capex $75-85B+
bullets.body: TSMC is expected to raise its FY26 revenue growth guidance from +40% to low-to-mid 40s%, with Q4 guiding up 10-15% q/q on sustained Blackwell demand. Multiple banks are raising TSMC capex estimates: GS TMT pegs 2027E at $85B (vs $78B prior) and 2028E at $98B. Additionally, TSMC is reportedly evaluating a second US fab cluster in Texas with up to six advanced wafer fabs, with Tesla/SpaceX in discussions for capacity — a move seen as a threat to Intel's foundry role.

bullets.title: MRVL Investor Day: $12B+ CY28 AI revenue target; $45B FY31 bull case
bullets.body: Marvell's investor day is the focal event today, with Piper expecting management to introduce a new LT model potentially stretching to FY31 with $45B revenue and ~$19 EPS (45% CAGR). OPCO and UBS both flag the XPU 'attach' opportunity as underappreciated — Google's $120B TPU deal cited as a proxy. UBS raised its MRVL PT to $335 (FY29E $30B rev/$12 EPS); however, UBS's Arcuri cautions crowded positioning and elevated buy-side hopes for >$20 EPS vs his $20 target could trigger a sell-the-news reaction.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure CapEx arms race: OpenAI at $1.4T valuation, DeepSeek $12B raise, server TAM +78% y/y
bullets.body: OpenAI is seeking $30B from UAE funds and BlackRock at a $1.4T valuation; DeepSeek is raising $12B+ backed by Tencent and CATL ahead of an early 2027 IPO; Moonshot AI is valued at $50B with $2B ARR expected by year-end. JPM's hardware model shows the server market expanding to $506B in 2026 from $284B in 2025 (+78% y/y), with AI server CAGR of +37% through 2030 and DC Ethernet switch market up +52% y/y to $48B. AI and pricing-fueled revisions drove all subsectors materially higher vs JPM's June 2026 outlook.

bullets.title: Behind-the-meter power: $240B TAM through 2029 as AI grid shortfall hits 77 GW
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley frames distributed/behind-the-meter (BTM) power as a structural architectural shift, not a bridge, as AI data center demand creates a 77 GW power shortfall through 2029. Total BTM TAM seen at ~120 GW ($240B) through 2029 (77 GW data center + 40 GW C&I). Bloom Energy's SOFC ranks #1 on MS's composite scorecard, BorgWarner turbine #2; MS upgraded BWA to Overweight at $95 PT with the distributed power unit targeted at ~$1.2B EBITDA by 2030 (35% of group total).

bullets.title: Rates regime: 10yr at 5.27% (24-year high); Goldman Monetary Policy Factor at most pessimistic in 3 decades
bullets.body: The 10-year UST yield sits at 5.27% — its highest since 2002 — yet equities remain near records, a tension multiple sources flag. Goldman's Monetary Policy Factor is at -8, near its most pessimistic level in three decades. CTA positioning swung from +2.35 standard deviations in August to -0.80 today, creating re-risking capacity. AI infrastructure median forward P/E compressed from 32x in April to 22x. Hedgeye flags Nasdaq recording more new lows than highs for 26 consecutive sessions despite index at record levels, and warns of headwinds from stronger dollar, higher rates, and credit pressure.

bullets.title: Hedgeye Quad2 framework: stay long USD, Tech (QQQ/XLK at ATH); exit bonds and IG/HY credit
bullets.body: Hedgeye is positioned for Quad2 (growth accelerating, inflation accelerating): stay long US tech and USD, exit long-duration Treasuries (LQD, HYG bearish). Expensive Software basket (SNOW +90%, NET +46%, TEAM +81% YTD) cited as top signal-strength names. SPX immediate risk range: 7651–7798 (bullish); COMPQ 26686–27550 (bullish). Historically in Quad2, Tech is the best equity sector and Fixed Income the worst asset class.

bullets.title: Inflation: Hedgeye nowcasts October CPI at +3.80% y/y; Wolfe sees September core at 0.22% MoM
bullets.body: Hedgeye's inflation nowcast puts October CPI at +3.80% y/y (+6bp from prior), with September at +3.74% y/y; the model has 90% directional accuracy. Wolfe separately forecasts September core CPI at 0.22% MoM (down from August's 0.29%), with airfares +2% MoM on jet fuel costs partially offset by lodging giveback. Market is only pricing a 22% probability of an October rate hike. Wolfe sees the risk to the CPI print as asymmetrically to the upside.

bullets.title: Memory supply tightening sharply: DRAM lead times 20 weeks, HDD 50 weeks; MU raises FY27 capex to $50B+
bullets.body: DRAM lead times have extended to 20 weeks and HDD lead times to 50 weeks per MS TMT, with the supply squeeze expected to worsen through 2027. Micron FQ1 guidance beat the Street; DRAM/NAND supply is constrained through C28, with bit growth in the low-20%/mid-20% range, and Micron raised FY27 capex guidance to $50B+. UBS also notes Micron sees tighter memory supply through FY28. Separately, Seagate and Toshiba are competing to acquire TDK's HDD magnetic-heads business in a deal worth several billion dollars.

bullets.title: S&P 500 breadth near 45-year low: only 24% of companies outperforming the index in September
bullets.body: Jefferies notes S&P 500 breadth degradation with only 24% of companies outperforming the index in September, near a 45-year low. Tech and Energy represent over 75% of YTD S&P 500 EPS revisions. Retail coverage is down 12% YTD vs S&P +14%. The GOOGL short vs. META long remains a popular multi-manager community narrative. US bond futures saw the largest weekly net buying in 5-year history ($89B) as dip-buyers were triggered by the rate sell-off.

bullets.title: Enterprise IT channel checks: 2027 pipeline forming unusually early; AI, cyber, and infra budgets not cannibalizing each other
bullets.body: JPM channel checks with a large US VAR show 2027 bookings well above expectations across Q1-Q3, with three distinct budget pools (AI, cybersecurity, infrastructure modernization) advancing simultaneously. Frontier-model security vulnerabilities are pulling projects forward and generating incremental non-discretionary budget. Agentic AI is driving substantially higher token consumption per workflow. Cisco is advantaged in hyperscale AI DC via NVIDIA partnership; AMD expected to gain share through 2027 with AMD-based architectures already in proposals.

bullets.title: Meta and Microsoft cutting Anthropic Claude usage by ~50%; META developing proprietary AI coding tools
bullets.body: Meta reduced internal Claude Code users from 60K to 30K and spent >$105M on Claude in a recent 28-day period; it is developing proprietary AI coding tools to reduce third-party model reliance and expects $5-10B total 3P model spend with potential cost savings next year. Microsoft is also cutting frontier model usage by more than one-third. Both moves are being cited as successful cost optimization, not capability gaps.

bullets.title: HUBS cuts 7% of workforce, raises FY30 op margin target to 30% (from 25%), reaffirms near-term guidance
bullets.body: HubSpot authorized a restructuring eliminating ~7% of its workforce effective October 1, with $65-75M in charges (mostly Q4 FY26). The company simultaneously raised its FY30 non-GAAP operating margin target to 30% from 25% and reaffirmed Q3 and FY26 guidance in line with FactSet consensus ($3.25-3.27 EPS, $924-925M revenue for Q3). Restructuring charges are excluded from non-GAAP results.

bullets.title: French bond rout highlights global fiscal fragility; US 30yr near 6% threatening credit dynamics
bullets.body: French political uncertainty triggered bond market repricing with government spending and taxes above 50% of GDP for 35 years; only Germany is on track to keep gross debt/GDP below 100% ahead. In the US, rising 30-year yields near 6% are threatening Treasury futures hedging dynamics and driving widening spreads that push borrowing costs for the weakest US companies to multi-year highs. Higher rates are expected to reduce 2027 US GDP growth by ~0.2pp, primarily through weaker residential investment.

bullets.title: Regional banks upgraded into Q3 earnings: M&T and KeyCorp to Outperform; Fed rate path pricing 4-5 hikes through YE27
bullets.body: 22V Research upgrades M&T Bank (PT $260) and KeyCorp (PT $24.50) to Sector Outperform ahead of Q3 earnings, citing NIM expansion, deposit stabilization, and asset sensitivity tailwinds. The Fed rate path is now priced at 4-5 hikes through YE27 vs. 3 previously, and the 3M/5Y curve steepened from ~55bps to ~95bps, positive for bank NII. Deposit pricing pressures are moderating from Q2, and agentic AI threat to deposits is seen as limited near-term.

bullets.title: BABA cloud revenue to grow 50%+ YoY in Sep-Q; T-Head chip contribution to rise from 10% to 40-50%
bullets.body: Jefferies reaffirms a bullish 2027 China internet outlook, forecasting BABA external cloud revenue to grow over 50% YoY in the September quarter with further acceleration in December and March quarters, reaching $100B by FY31 and $160B by FY33 (40-45% CAGR). T-Head cumulative shipments hit 560K by April 2026 with V900/J900 releases planned for 1Q27/3Q28; T-Head's share of internal compute is expected to rise from 10% to 40-50%. China's National Day holiday (Oct 1-5) showed no major positive surprises, with movie box office down 32% YoY.

bullets.title: Euozone macro weak: German factory orders -10.6%; Chinese brands take 13.1% of W. Europe auto market
bullets.body: German industrial orders fell 10.6% MoM in August, far worse than the 1% drop expected, though the decline was bulk-order driven (aircraft, military); ex-bulk orders were flat. Separately, Chinese auto brands captured 13.1% of Western Europe's passenger vehicle market in August (+5.5ppt YoY), with NEV share rising to 22.7% (+6.5ppt) while German brands lost 3.3ppt. BYD moved to #1 among Chinese NEV players at 31% share. EU tariff finalization may not occur until end-2026.
